title: Lo the Young Tribes of Adam Rise
description: Lo the Young Tribes of Adam Rise in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 90, headed “The same”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lo the young tribes of A-dam rise, And thro' all na-ture rove, Ful-fil the wish-es of their eyes, And taste the joys they love.

lines: Lo the young tribes of Adam rise,
Fulfil the wishes of their eyes,
And taste the joys they love.
They give a loose to wild desires,
The strict account that God requires
Of all the works they do.
The Judge prepares his throne on high,
Avoid the fury of his eye,
How shall I bear that dreadful day,
I give all mortal joys away

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
